name: Mermaid waves

card.summary: A long, loose, beachy wavy hairstyle trend that adds volume and soft movement to long hair, framing the face with a relaxed look.
card.note: A styling trend; heat tools used to create waves can damage hair.

quick.overview:
Mermaid waves are a trend of long hair worn in loose, flowing waves, giving a beachy, fluid look with volume and movement. The look is used to add texture and softness to straight or flat hair and to frame the face.

It is a fashion style rather than a procedure, and no studies have examined it. Its effect on appearance is documented through styling practice and social media trends.
quick.how: Waves are typically made by curling or waving long hair with a curling iron or wand, by braiding or twisting damp hair and letting it dry, or by other heatless methods, then finishing with texturizing products. People with naturally wavy hair may enhance their pattern instead. The style lasts until the next wash.
quick.risks: Heat tools can damage hair, and Wikipedia's hairstyle article notes heat-protection products are recommended with curling irons and flat irons [1]. Tight braids worn for too long can cause traction alopecia [1].

lead: Mermaid waves are a long wavy hairstyle trend: loose waves running through the length of the hair, associated with a beachy look. As a style, it falls under hairstyling in general, which involves changing hair's length, texture, shape or arrangement as part of grooming and fashion [1].

People use waves to add volume and movement to long hair. Curling and waving are done with heat tools or by shaping hair while damp; Wikipedia notes that curling irons and flat irons use heat to create waves, curls or temporary straightness, and that heat can damage hair [1]. The style is a trend term used in beauty media rather than a technical hairdressing category, and no studies examine it.

paras: Mermaid waves describe long hair worn in soft, flowing waves. As a hairstyle, it is part of the broader practice of styling hair to change its shape and texture [1].

Waves are made by curling or waving with heated tools, which can damage hair so heat-protection products are recommended [1], or by shaping damp hair with braids and letting it air-dry. Wikipedia warns that tight braiding can cause traction alopecia if left in too long [1].
